title: A Union Without an Employer: SEWA's Registration in 1972
industry: labour organising (trade union and cooperative finance)
conflicts: Membership within three years: over 5,000 (Magsaysay Foundation, 1977) versus 7,000 (Right Livelihood); story gives both, attributed. SEWA Bank founding year: 1974 (SEWA, Right Livelihood) versus 1972 and 1973 (two places on The Elders' profile); story uses 1974.
notes: Episode changed from the slate's SEWA Bank founding (1974) to SEWA's own founding and trade-union registration (1971-72), with the bank as a sequel: the shared web-search budget ran out before any loadable source describing the bank's founding meeting could be found (SEWA Bank's site has an expired certificate). The 1971 cloth-market narrative rests on SEWA's own history page, signalled as SEWA's account; registration and its difficulty are independently confirmed by Right Livelihood and the Magsaysay Foundation. Industry shifts from finance to labour organising; an editor wanting a finance slot could revisit the bank episode with Bhatt's book 'We Are Poor but So Many'. Quote stance: complicates.
